exposure: Head to perineum distance (HPD) measured serially
outcome: Mode of birth (vaginal delivery or cesarean section)
cohort: The study included 299 nulliparous and multiparous patients during the first stage of labor.
finding: Serial measurements of Head to perineum distance (HPD) and Angle of progression (AOP) during the first stage of labor predict cesarean section, with AOP demonstrating superior predictive ability compared to HPD.
mod_finding: Slower changes in HPD and AOP values were detected in patients who underwent cesarean section, with specific thresholds for both markers predicting the need for cesarean section with high sensitivity.
